title: Runtime query planner cost model and hedging controller for dashboard API
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: The Console dashboard query API experiences variable tail latency under bursty tenant workloads. Current heuristics for when to run read hedging and how to size internal caches are static and lead to either over-hedging (extra load & cost) or under-hedging (high tail latency).

Goal: Implement a lightweight runtime query planner with a learned cost model and a hedging controller that: (1) predicts per-query expected cost/latency given current cache hit rates and request features, (2) decides whether to hedge or shed requests, and (3) adjusts cache eviction and admission policies dynamically to optimize tail latency vs. cost.

Scope: prototype in Console query-router service (Go) for top-100 dashboard endpoints + backend metrics pipeline integration to feed feature signals (recent latency, cache hit ratios, tenant priority). MVP will not change storage engine; it will emit telemetry and have toggles for canary.

Non‑goals: reworking storage indexing or sharding for this ticket. No changes to public API surface.

Success metrics (measured on dedicated canary tenants):
- 95th percentile query latency reduction >= 25% during burst windows
- Overall CPU/GPU cost increase <= 5% for hedging actions
- False-positive hedging (unnecessary duplicate reads) rate < 10% of hedged decisions

Acceptance criteria:
- New cost model component deployed behind feature flag; model retrains on rolling window and logs scores
- Hedging controller runs per-request and produces stable decisions with telemetry stored in Prometheus + tracing spans in Zipkin
- New cache admission/eviction knobs wired to runtime controller and shown in Console dashboard
acceptance_criteria: Cost model produces per-request cost/latency score and is logged for >95% of sampled requests
Hedging controller implements threshold policy with configurable override and is toggleable per-tenant
End-to-end canary run shows 95th latency reduced by >=25% for canary tenants under simulated bursts
Dashboards/graphs updated to visualize hedging decisions, cache hit ratio, and additional cost
Implementation has unit tests and an integration test simulating bursty tenant traffic
implementation_notes: Implement cost model as lightweight linear-regression + exponential moving average features to keep runtime CPU low. Training job runs in pipeline weekly and outputs coefficients to service config. Hedging controller uses sliding-window percentile estimates and a tunable utility function (latency benefit vs. extra read cost). Start with conservative thresholds and add automatic cooldown to avoid oscillation.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Hedging may overload origin when misconfigured. Mitigation: add global throttles and circuit-breaker with automatic backoff.
Risk: Model drift causing poor decisions. Mitigation: enable telemetry, replay logs for offline validation, and quick rollback flag.
Risk: Increased SLO violations for other tenants due to hedging. Mitigation: per-tenant budget and priority-aware admission control.
testing_plan: Local harness to simulate 5000 req/s with configurable burst shapes. Integration tests in staging that run for 48h with synthetic tenants and compare baseline vs. controller-on traces. Load test results are recorded in Google Drive artifact linked below.
